title: Secondary Elementary Mathematics Scheme of Work: Algebra and Functions
subject: math
overview: This guide covers the Algebra and functions unit (Term 1): e-numbers, e-algebra, e-functions-graphs.
Work through the key ideas first, follow the revision plan day by day, watch out for the traps, and try the questions together at home.

keyIdeas.explanation: Multiplying out brackets so every term in one bracket multiplies every term in the other: (x + 2)(x + 3) expands to x^2 + 5x + 6.
Writing an expression as a product of brackets, the reverse of expansion: 2x + 6 + xy + 3y factorises to (x + 3)(2 + y).
The variable a formula is rearranged to give on its own: in x = (y - 5) / 3, taken from y = 3x + 5, the subject is x.
A statement that is true for every value of the variables, like (a + b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2, unlike an equation that holds only for some values.

revisionPlan.focus: Practice set for e-algebra: Make x the subject of y = 3x + 7.

traps.watchFor: The same-base index rule is for multiplying, but it gets misapplied to addition. The index rule is for multiplying, never adding: 8 + 16 = 24, not 128. In class, put the two questions side by side: multiplying joins the factors so the indices add (2^3 x 2^4 = 2^7 = 128), but adding keeps the powers separate, so work out 8 and 16 first.

The power looks like it lands on each term of the sum. That is why the two-term answer feels right, but expanding the whole bracket gives three terms. The full expansion has three terms: check a = 2, b = 3, and 25 is not 13. In class, expand (a + b)(a + b) with the area model so the middle term 2ab is visible as a region.

traps.misconception: The line with the bigger intercept is steeper.
traps.watchFor: The intercept is the visible height, so it feels like the climb. That is why the higher-starting line feels steeper, but height is not climb. Steepness is the gradient, not the intercept: compare m, never c. In class, compare y = 4x − 6 with y = x + 3: the first starts lower yet rises four times as fast.
